0.0.n: Introduces the next item or category being discussed.

0.1.n: Marks 次 as the topic, shifting attention to what comes next.

0.2.n: Softens the introduction rather than specifying an exact amount.

0.3.n: Combines with 部門 to identify the bakery category.

0.4.n: Refers to a product category, here bread and bakery items.

0.5.n: Adds the bread category to other categories already discussed.

0.6.n: Expresses that something exists or is available.

0.7.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before です.

0.8.n: Makes the explanation with ん polite.

0.9.n: Gently leads into the next statement without necessarily expressing a contrast.

1.0.n: Points to the product the speaker is introducing.

1.1.n: Suggests another item mentioned earlier was newly released too.

1.2.n: A noun describing a product that has just gone on sale.

1.3.n: The connecting form of だ, linking this description to the next statement.

2.0.n: Names the flavor of the bread here.

2.1.n: Links coffee to French bread, indicating its flavor rather than ownership.

2.2.n: A compound noun referring to French-style bread, often baguette-like.

2.3.n: Politely identifies the product after a noun.

3.0.n: Refers to an earlier occasion when the speaker tried another version.

3.1.n: Marks 以前 as the time of the earlier experience.

3.2.n: Combines with バター to name the earlier bread's filling or flavor.

3.3.n: Pairs with あん in the popular sweet bean paste and butter combination.

3.4.n: だっ is the part of だ used before た to form だった.

3.5.n: Completes だった, placing the identification of the earlier flavor in the past.

3.6.n: Works with な to express uncertainty while recalling the earlier flavor.

3.7.n: With か, creates かな, a gentle question the speaker asks themself.

3.9.n: Refers back to the earlier bean paste and butter product.

3.10.n: Includes the earlier product among things the speaker found tasty.

3.11.n: Past form of 美味しい, made by replacing the final い with かった.

3.12.n: Here it means a remembered impression, not a visual picture.

3.13.n: Marks イメージ as what the speaker had.

3.14.n: Past form of ある; an impression existed, naturally expressed in English as having an impression.

3.15.n: Connects the positive memory to the reason for buying today's product.

4.0.n: Sets the time of the current purchase.

4.1.n: Shows that today's purchase repeats an earlier pattern.

4.2.n: Casual form of やはり, suggesting the choice fits the speaker's usual preferences.

4.3.n: Negative connecting form of 外せる, expressing inability to leave this item out of the purchases.

4.4.m: ended up buying and bringing back
4.4.n: 買ってくる means buy and bring back; てしまいました adds a polite past sense of giving in.

0.lit: Next, there is also a little bread section, though.
0.tip: んですけど softens an introduction and leaves room for the explanation that follows.

1.lit: This too is a new release, and…
1.tip: で connects a noun-based statement to the next clause instead of ending it with です.

2.tip: の can connect a flavor to a food, not just show possession.

3.lit: Previously, was it bean paste butter, I wonder; I had the impression that one too was delicious, so…
3.tip: だったかな signals that the speaker is checking their own memory rather than confidently naming the earlier flavor.

4.lit: Today too, as expected, I couldn't leave it out and ended up buying and bringing it back.
4.tip: てしまいました can suggest giving in to temptation, without expressing serious regret.
